School Opening Hours
The school gates open at 8:40am registration closes at 8.50am. The school day finishes at 3:15pm for Early Years and KS1 and 3.20pm for KS2. This is 32.5 hours per week.
Morning session: 9.00am to 12.00pm for KS1 and 12:20pm for KS2
Afternoon session:1:00pm to 3:15pm for Early Years and KS1 and 1.20pm to 3.20pm for KS2
Breakfast Club: 8.00am - 8.40am
After School Club: 3:15pm to 5:30pm.
Any children that are late to school will be recorded as absent if after 9.20 am and late if before this time. This will affect your child's overall attendance. The school keeps daily records of any lateness.
If you are going to be late collecting your child then please let the school office know. If you are persistently late collecting your child from school you may be charged an After School Club fee of £7.50 for the time.
School Opening Hours

Governors
Welcome to our Governors’ section.
Please find below details of how our Governing body is structured, including the names, categories, responsibilities and terms of appointment for each Governor.
A school can have between 9 and 20 governors who are collectively known as the governing body. The Preston and Wingham Primary Schools Federation has one Governing Body school. The governing body works with the staff to develop the vision, values and ethos of the federation and the schools within it. They support and challenge the federation to continuously review, evaluate and develop its systems and provision to enable all pupils to achieve the very best education in a safe and secure environment and consequently achieve all that they are capable of.
The governing body of The Preston & Wingham Primary Schools Federation has 12 members, made up as follows:
The governing body of The Preston & Wingham Primary Schools Federation works to the circle model of governance.

One of these options is learning to play a musical instrument, we are very lucky to have two different music teachers who come into school and give private lessons. Parents Information
We strongly believe that the children can only achieve their best from their time here at Wingham School, if there is a strong and supportive partnership between school and parent. There are two formal parent teacher consultations during the year. Parents will also receive a written annual report at the end of the academic year. Parents will also be invited into school at set times during the year to spend time in the classroom, learning alongside their children.
The school office is the first point of contact for all general enquiries. Your child's class teacher will handle any queries relating specifically to learning, and will be pleased to meet with you after school - preferably by prior appointment made through the school office. Where concerns cannot be addressed through these channels, the Head of School is happy to assist – again, by prior appointment.

SEND
Inclusion
We aim to ensure that every child in our school has access to a broad and exciting curriculum, a range of extra curricula activities and a safe, supportive environment to thrive and grow both academically and also emotionally. This is regardless of gender, race or ability.
To ensure that all children at the school are given the opportunities to succeed and the tools to grow and thrive we recognise that some children will need extra support to achieve this. We also recognise that there will be children who come from disadvantaged backgrounds and it is our responsibility to ensure they given the chances and support to make good progress and develop socially, academically and emotionally.
To achieve all of this the school uses different support programmes, employs members of support staff and ensures that all inclusion related activities begin in the classroom with highly effective and supportive teaching. If we use an intervention to support your child it has been chosen because of its known effectivness though research and evidence: https://educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk/
Hopefully the information on the website will help to answer most of the questions you may have but, if not, please do not hesitate to contact me.
Ms Douglas is the Inclusion Leader for the Federation and provides oversight and direction in this area.
To contact Ms Douglas email: office@winghamprimary.co.uk

Curriculum
At Preston and Wingham Primary school federation we are all learners together. We believe that children should have the opportunity to acquire the necessary knowledge and skills to become life-long learners.
We strive to provide a curriculum for our children that is ‘rich and memorable’. Through a rich and creative approach to the national curriculum, key texts that have been carefully curated, we deepen understanding and encourage mastery. We facilitate opportunities for children to learn and remember things; to gain and build essential knowledge and skills through a wealth of interconnected themes that can be applied to all aspects of life in, and beyond, the primary classroom. Topics are carefully chosen to enthuse and engage learners, develop a secure understanding and build a range of transferable skills.
At the heart of our curriculum is a commitment to nurture a love of reading as this opens the door to all learning; books form the foundations of topics and all pupils are encouraged to read widely, developing an extensive vocabulary, sound comprehension skills and a voracious appetite for books.
At Preston and Wingham Primary school federation we promote, celebrate and nurture children's abilities to make choices with their learning. We understand that children have strengths in many areas and these are encouraged and explored. This belief continues into our assessment of foundation subjects. Our unique way of assessment is called FLOURISH. Click on the hyperlink or see the star below for more details.
Our aim is simple; to enable children to become life-long learners who respect universal human values, are internationally and culturally minded and who have an acute awareness of themselves, their community and the ever-changing world around them.

School Clubs
At Wingham we run many extra-curricular clubs during the year including, football club, art, choir, yoga, gymnastics, coding, rugby, cricket, dance.
We want to ensure our clubs are accessible to all and encourage everyone to book onto a club. The cost for a 6 week club is £5 and there is no fee for children who are eligible for Free School Meals (FSM).
All clubs will run until 4.15 pm. Please arrive promptly to pick your children up as the teachers still have marking, planning and preparation to do afterwards which they cannot start until all the children in their club have left.
The Breakfast Club is open every weekday from 8:00am to 8:45am during term time. The CASH club runs from 3.15-5.30. The clubs provide quality care for the pupils of Wingham Primary School enabling parents/carers to work or study beyond statutory school hours.
We aim to provide a happy, safe, warm and stimulating environment for our children.
All CASH Club spaces must be pre-booked.
For further information please contact the school office.

Global Citizenship
“Education for global citizenship helps enable young people to develop the core competencies which allow them to actively engage with the world, and help to make it a more just and sustainable place.”
At Wingham Primary School, we strongly believe in developing children as Global Citizens, who actively engage in activities to bring about positive social change.
This page has been dedicated to the various activities that take place within the school, in relation to this aspect of our ethos. Please check back regularly to see how the students are being educated about the rights of children and how they are supporting others to access their rights locally, nationally and globally.
Why is China important to our world? What are the similarities and differences to our life in Britain?
We learnt about the Chinese celebration: Luna New Year. We learnt how to do traditional Chinese dancing: dragon, fans and parasoles.
In assembly, we explored China's exports and discovered cars, electricals and toys are exported to the UK.
We learnt that the Chinese alphabet is made up of symbols and we made bookmarks.
We explored the landscape of China and the cities. We watched a film about school life and saw that playtime looks very different. Students do aerobics during morning break and do their homework at lunch break!
“Why do some people and animals move from one country to another, and what are some reasons they might decide to live in a new place?”
Exploring migration, borders, what it means to leave one’s home.
Recognising the courage, fear, uncertainty that many displaced people face.
Developing an understanding that migration is complex, and while it involves danger, hardship, it’s often driven by the hope for safety and a better life.
Education for global citizenship supports young people to explore and question the world around them. It promotes critical thinking, advocates social justice and encourages learners to apply their learning to real world issues.
Year 4 Letters and presentation to Sir Roger Gale about children around the world and their access to drinking water.

OFSTED
Please find below our most recent Ofsted report and relevant information from the Department for Education Performance Tables.
Previously, schools received a single overall judgement such as Outstanding, Good, or Requires Improvement. Under the new framework, this approach has been replaced with report cards that break down performance into key areas that Ofsted says matter most to families:
Safeguarding will also be clearly marked as ‘Met’ or ‘Not Met’.
Previously, schools were assigned a single overall grade. The updated system, however, offers a multi-dimensional perspective, highlighting both strengths and areas for improvement within the same school. As a result, a school might be at the Expected Standard in one aspect but Needs Attention in another, giving parents a clearer sense of their children's experience at the school. Since the new grading method and criteria differ entirely from the old system, Ofsted says that previous judgements such as Good or Outstanding cannot be directly mapped onto the new categories and grades.
There is a strong nationwide focus on inclusion, ensuring every child’s needs are met and a renewed emphasis on attendance, recognising its vital role in achievement and wellbeing. These priorities are already central to our work.

Early Years
We plan provision so that:
Our RICH values are reflected in our school ethos and embedded within our Early Years curriculum.
We show Respect for our environment and our friends and those in our school.
We are Inclusive thinking about the needs of others and that we are all different but valued equally.
We are Creative with our minds and thinking, we ask questions and are curious. We study artists and composers and create our own masterpieces.
We are Hardworking trying our very best even though it may be challenging.
Our high quality adult interactions with the children enhance learning and development whilst following the children's lead. Our aim is to provide our children with knowledge, skills and experiences in a hands on holistic way so that learning is embedded in a meaningful context.
Our children’s physical and mental wellbeing is important to us and we teach them important self-regulation techniques and how to make and build positive relationships right from when they join us. We use Heartsmart which is a creative approach to build character, emotional health and resilience in our children. The Thrive approach is adopted throughout from the outset ensuring we are meeting the emotional needs of all our children. We want our children to be tolerant of others and understand the need for kindness, empathy and respect. This is threaded throughout our daily teaching and alongside this our children learn about different religions, cultures and places of worship.
Children are full of such wonder and curiosity and it's marvellous to see that flourish as they start their learning journey with us at Wingham. We want to nurture that curiosity , feed their imagination and excite them with their learning.
